items.title: Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket over consumer protection laws
items.content_text: - **Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket over consumer protection laws** — Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott and the City Council filed lawsuits against Kalshi, Polymarket and affiliated companies, alleging they violated the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance by operating unlicensed sports betting platforms and misleading consumers about the legality of their products. The suits allege the platforms offer game-winner, spread and player-prop wagers rebranded as event contracts to avoid state licensing, taxes and responsible-gambling rules. items.title: CFTC moves to define prediction-market event contracts as swaps, excludes casino-style gambling
items.content_text: - **CFTC moves to define prediction-market event contracts as swaps, excludes casino-style gambling** — The CFTC on October 9 issued an interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling from the definition of a swap and a companion proposal to explicitly classify event contracts tied to sports, politics, culture and weather as swaps. Chairman Selig says the contracts are commodity derivatives within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction; the move comes as the state-federal fight heads toward the Supreme Court.
